answer: When k coordinated identities equivocate on the same consensus commitment, verified correlation triggers a penalty proportional to k², charged against bonded escrows rather than only each key’s stake. Detection also applies asymmetric depreciation: linked exposure compounds capital loss by an exponential multiplier, making a sybil swarm costlier than isolated faults. There is no haven in forged identities: a trellis of colluding keys increases auditable liability.
